items.title: Node2Shell: Reproducing CVE-2026-111497 in the Node.js Brotli decoder
items.summary: We reproduced CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js and other runtimes, and explain how to detect and remediate it.

items.title: Code security for new coders
items.summary: This post breaks down essential code security terms and tools so that you can build safely from the start.

items.title: PHP2Shell - Critical vulnerabilities in PHP (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619): detection, analysis, and remediation
items.summary: Learn about the two critical vulnerabilities in PHP dubbed PHP2Shell.

items.title: LiteLLM supply chain compromise: What you need to know
items.summary: Malicious releases of LiteLLM v1.107.0 were published to PyPI and container registries following multiple maintainer account compromises.

items.title: Introducing pathrunner: An AWS privilege escalation framework
items.summary: Introducing pathrunner, a modular, cloud-native offensive security framework that automates the exploitation of AWS IAM privilege escalation paths.

items.title: Putting models to the secure coding test: Security rules
items.summary: We tested Sonnet 5, Composer 2.5, and GPT 5.5 using set security rules to see whether using them produces measurably more secure code.

items.title: Jev as a judge: How counterfeit policy steers Jev
items.summary: We evaluate Jev's prompt injection detection and show how counterfeit classification policies can steer its decisions and bypass LangChain's tool-risk gating.

items.title: Beyond valid credentials: How exposed AWS keys are tested for Amazon Bedrock access
items.summary: In this post, we share LLM-specific validation patterns that attackers use to test exposed AWS credentials for Amazon Bedrock access.

items.title: Guarding the gates: Assessing dangerous permissions granted to Kubernetes built-in principals
items.summary: We analyzed RBAC bindings across over 65,000 Kubernetes clusters to find dangerous permissions granted to system:anonymous, system:unauthenticated, and system:authenticated.

items.title: Discovering and exploiting a remote code execution vulnerability in OpenCode (GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4)
items.summary: Datadog Security Labs discovered GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4, a vulnerability in OpenCode's upgrade endpoint that, under certain conditions, allowed malicious webpages to execute code on developers' machines.

items.title: Attacker infrastructure, but vibe-coded: tracking the evolution of credential harvesting platforms
items.summary: In this post, we examine two vibe-coded credential harvesting platforms, Loot and UltraVault, and the Amazon Bedrock abuse used to validate stolen secrets.

items.title: Mapping out your unknown: A threat hunter’s guide to GitHub
items.summary: In this post, we walk through different threats to GitHub and how to detect them.

items.title: Password spraying campaign targets AWS root user accounts across 150+ organizations
items.summary: Datadog Security Research observed a password spraying campaign attempting to authenticate as the AWS root user across more than 150 organizations.

items.title: N4D Mesh Controller: New infrastructure, a UPX-packed agent labeled "go-titan," and how to hunt for it
items.summary: Datadog Security Research executed a newer N4D Mesh Controller sample in isolated microVMs, uncovering rotated infrastructure, a UPX-packed go-titan agent, MCP tool abuse in action, and direct runtime evidence of multi-service scanning and persistence.

items.title: Putting models to the secure coding test: Plan vs default mode
items.summary: We tested Sonnet 5, Composer 2.5, and GPT 5.5 in plan mode and default mode to see whether plan mode produces measurably more secure code.

items.title: 'ChainDrop' worm compromises hundreds of popular npm packages
items.summary: On August 4, 2026, several popular npm packages, including 'keyv', were compromised to deliver malware.

items.title: Before the first prompt: Code execution paths in trusted coding-agent projects
items.summary: Learn how trusted coding-agent projects can execute repository-controlled code before the first prompt through Codex MCP configuration and Claude Code environment settings.

items.title: Detection primitives for eBPF rootkits
items.summary: We analyze how VoidLink, LinkPro, and Atomic Arch abuse eBPF helpers to hide from defenders, and show how to detect them at load time, before they can act.

items.title: Compromised AsyncAPI npm packages: inside a CI supply-chain attack
items.summary: On July 14, 2026, four npm packages in the @asyncapi namespace, totaling over 3 million weekly downloads, were compromised to deliver credential-stealing malware. We investigate how the attack unfolded and how to know if you're affected.

items.title: Not-so-anonymous telemetry: The @injectivelabs/sdk-ts backdoor
items.summary: A malicious commit disguised as SDK telemetry briefly compromised @injectivelabs/sdk-ts, exfiltrating wallet mnemonics and private keys.

items.title: Coordinated GitHub API enumeration and access token abuse
items.summary: Datadog Security Research has tracked multiple coordinated campaigns enumerating GitHub organizations, repositories, and users through the public GitHub API, abusing leaked access tokens, and cloning private repositories.

items.title: Entra Agent ID: Protect, detect, respond
items.summary: This post continues and concludes our series on Agent ID, by outlining steps that an administrator or security team can take to secure blueprints and agent identities created in their local Entra ID tenant.

items.title: Backdoors & Breaches: New scenarios and adaptations
items.summary: Sharing new scenarios and adaptations to play the Datadog expansion pack of Backdoors & Breaches.

items.title: Introducing GuardDog 3.0: A new rules engine, transparent sandboxing, and more
items.summary: Release of GuardDog 3.0, an open-source tool to identify malicious packages, featuring a new YARA-based rules engine, a risk scoring engine, and built-in sandboxing.

items.title: Behind the console: An AiTM phishing kit harvesting AWS console credentials and beyond
items.summary: Datadog Security Research investigates a June 2026 adversary-in-the-middle phishing campaign that cloned the AWS console login page to harvest victim credentials and multi-factor authentication codes.

items.title: Detecting the Klue supply chain attack in Salesforce instances
items.summary: We summarize the Klue supply chain attack and provide detection guidance for Salesforce environments monitored by Datadog Cloud SIEM.

items.title: Entra Agent ID: Inside a cross-tenant agent compromise
items.summary: Continuing our Agent ID series, this post demonstrates how a privileged agent could be compromised through its third-party blueprint. This leads to a cross-tenant incident similar to Midnight Blizzard, since an attacker with control over an agent blueprint can authenticate as any agent associated with that blueprint.

items.title: Mapping out your unknown: A threat hunter’s guide to Salesforce
items.summary: In this post, we walk through different threats to Salesforce and how to detect them.

items.title: Holding blobs for ransom: Four methods for Azure Storage ransomware
items.summary: This post explores four vectors for threat actors to abuse Azure Storage to maliciously encrypt victim blobs, including step-by-step explanations and event codes for detection.

items.title: Entra Agent ID: The blueprint blast radius
items.summary: Entra Agent ID is an extension of Entra's application model that provides identities for AI agents. Unlike applications, the agent identity model allows linking a single app registration (blueprint) to multiple identities and their associated privileges, increasing the potential blast radius of a compromised agent.
